content_md: We already saw this with DAOs and crypto orgs, but AI is reinforcing the same lessons — minimum-viable corporate structures that are legible to governments and able to sustain legal, tax-compliant existence are ridiculously cumbersome. 2-3 people with high trust can just collaborate informally but more people or lower trust equals huge barriers. Like crypto, AI in theory allows very small-scale and low-overhead ops of many kinds. Almost everything scales down in size, and can become faster and more agile in time. The only thing that doesn’t is relationships with states. The limiting factor is the resolution of “seeing like a state.” A part of this is technological, but a bigger part is that political power *likes* scale. A society that has power and resources aggregated in medium to large to very large chunks makes governance easier and highly profitable to those who govern. Small and very small chunks are less attractive and require a genuine service motive to even want to govern.
